brief_improvements: The 'compose by name, not by copy' rule (author-brief item 2, sharpened after ceremony 2) is still being missed inconsistently within one wave: two of the eight wave-2 skills (cap-document-validation-implement for F-b1-08/F-b4-01, cap-errors-implement for F-a7-04) restate an agentic-stack finding with no attribution, while sibling skills in the same wave state the identical fact correctly by name. Add a mechanical pre-flight check to the author brief: before closing a skill.json, grep its own file for every F-a7-* and F-b1-* id it cites, and for each one confirm the word 'agentic-stack' (or the owning skill's name) appears within 200 characters of that id's row -- not just once per skill, but once per citation, since C3-002 shows the same skill can cite a finding once correctly and once without attribution.

The instruction-count budget (6 to 10) is a checked ceiling but nothing enforces it at write time; two of eight wave-2 skills landed at 11. Consider adding a warning (not yet an error) to tools/validate_skills.py for instructions/invariants/best_practices counts outside the stated budget, the same way it already warns on fewer than 3 instructions, so an author sees the overrun before the ceremony does.

cap-errors-use's self-contradiction on entry-point count (three named, four claimed) survived because the row was written independently of the instructions section that gets the same fact right later in the same file. When a skill states a fact TARGET.md enumerates (T1's three entry types versus T6's four), write it once as a shape or explicit list and have every other row point to that one enumeration, rather than re-listing the members each time a row needs them.
what_worked: python3 tools/validate_skills.py reports 0 errors across all 15 skills currently in the repo (112 warnings, all 'manifest lists X but it is not written yet' for future waves) -- every sourced quote in the eight wave-2 skills is a verified verbatim substring of its cited record, and every composes_with link matches docs/skill-manifest.json symmetrically, including cap-errors's and cap-document-validation's large used_by lists.

Both definitions of done labelled measured were independently re-run in this review and reproduced their recorded output exactly: build-simplicity-budget's counting script gave 'first_run_concepts 10 resident_metadata 9 minimum_implementation 9 verdict within' on the real schemas and 'verdict exceeded' with exit 1 on the recorded breakage; cap-errors-use's `bash examples/end-to-end/test.sh` gave 'passed 29, failed 0' clean and, with run.py's fail() edited exactly as the breakage describes, gave 'passed 25, failed 4' with the same four named failures and the same surviving 'names the missing field' line the skill records. Both skills wrote a criterion someone else could run from the skill alone, the practice ceremony 1 and 2 asked to be kept.

Every 'claimed' definition of done in this wave is honestly claimed: no tool that does not exist is described as having produced a result, and every claimed row says in its own expected_failure field why (typed errors absent, adapter not built, tool not written).
